entities.summary:
Georgia Tech, officially known as the Georgia Institute of Technology, is a prominent public research university founded in 1885 in Atlanta, Georgia, United States. It emerged as part of the Industrial Revolution's push for technological education, reflecting a growing recognition of the importance of engineering and applied sciences in the modern world. As a member of the University System of Georgia, Georgia Tech plays a crucial role in higher education and technological advancement in North America, influencing the region's economy and workforce.

Throughout its history, Georgia Tech has undergone significant transformations, including its designation as a technological university in the early 20th century and its expansion into various research domains. The institution played a pivotal role during World War II, contributing to advancements in aeronautics and military engineering. Notable alumni include Nobel Prize winners and influential figures in technology and business, such as former Governor of Georgia Nathan Deal and telecommunications pioneer John E. McDonald. By the late 20th century, Georgia Tech had established itself as a leader in engineering, computer science, and business education, integrating research with practical applications.

The legacy of Georgia Tech extends far beyond its physical campus, as it has contributed significantly to the development of the modern technology landscape. The emphasis on innovation and entrepreneurship has fostered a culture of startups and technological advancement within the Atlanta metropolitan area, resulting in a thriving ecosystem for new ventures. Companies like AT&T and Coca-Cola, which have historical ties to the region, have also benefited from the skilled workforce produced by Georgia Tech. This institution continues to shape future generations of engineers and leaders, making a lasting impact on society and the economy.
